summary: Timebound access request for de-identified inference payloads for calibration study
description:
Issue summary: Research team requests short-term access to a sampled, de-identified set of production inference payloads to calibrate a new hallucination-detection scoring heuristic.

Impact: Low risk to live production; moderate privacy risk if PII is not successfully removed. This request is time-sensitive for an upcoming conference demo but must follow privacy guardrails.

Request details: Access to sampled tokenized prompts and model responses (no raw user metadata) for a 48-hour window. Samples should be drawn from production ingestion between 2026-03-08T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-10T23:59:59Z, with a sampling rate ~5% stratified by endpoint and latency buckets.

What is being requested: Short-lived read-only mount of the sampled payload set to the research team's ephemeral workspace; IAM role to be scoped and time-limited; automated redaction/hash of any PII tokens prior to provisioning.

Rationale/justification: Model calibration to reduce false-positive hallucination alerts; internal research (no customer-facing publication planned beyond anonymized metrics). The new scoring heuristic requires realistic, anonymized model outputs to tune thresholds.

Expected deliverables: A short report summarizing calibration results, metrics before/after thresholding, and a statement confirming no re-identifiable data was retained.

Compliance constraints: Must adhere to data minimization SOP, Security's ephemeral-access playbook, and Privacy review sign-off. No raw session IDs, no IPs, and no attachments containing customer files to be included in the dataset.
justification: Model calibration to evaluate hallucination rates on real in-domain prompts; engineering research team needs limited traces to validate a new scoring heuristic.
data_minimization_plan: Provide only tokenized prompts and model responses; run automated PII filter to redact/hash flagged tokens; remove user identifiers, IPs, auth tokens, and session IDs; sample 5% of sessions using stratified sampling by endpoint/latency; store results in ephemeral S3 bucket with 48-hour TTL; no external downloads allowed.
access_controls: Grant short-lived IAM role (duration = 4 hours) bound to researcher identities, require MFA, apply read-only S3 policy, restrict network egress, log every read to audit index, and require signed acknowledgement of data handling by each researcher.
audit_and_logging: All provisioning events and object reads will be recorded in CloudTrail and forwarded to the audit index; object access will emit datapoints with requester, timestamp, and object key; audit logs retained for 90 days; security will run a short review within 24 hours of access completion.
steps_to_provision: 1) Research sends finalized sampling selector and filter config in this ticket.
2) Privacy runs automated PII policy on selector to confirm redaction coverage.
3) SRE creates ephemeral S3 bucket with lifecycle policy and scoped IAM role.
4) Data engineering runs extraction job, applies redaction filter, and writes tokenized samples to bucket.
5) Security performs quick sanity scan and signs off in ticket comments.
6) IAM role credentials issued via short-lived STS tokens and distributed to approved researcher IDs.
7) After 48 hours bucket is auto-deleted; security validates deletion and posts confirmation.
